circuit: copy of testcase/test26/test26.v (cone of n8[0]: depth 11, 63 gates)
purpose: Transform routing on a CONE: convert it, then optimise it. The catalog carries a 'cone CONVERSION vs cone OPTIMIZATION' block because the two share both the scope and most of the wording.

lines.prompt: How tall is the logic stack behind n8[0]?
lines.why_hard: Baseline for line 6; cone_gate_count returns 63 on the same net.

lines.prompt: Rebuild just that output's logic so it uses nothing but NAND and NOT cells.
lines.why_correct: A basis remap scoped to one cone: convert_basis carries the optional scope.
lines.why_hard: Dropping scope remaps all 1629 gates instead of the 63 in the cone, and still reports success. 'Just that output's logic' is the only thing holding the scope.

lines.prompt: Leaving the rest of the design untouched, make the logic behind n8[0] as shallow as you can.
lines.why_hard: The net is named and 'leaving the rest of the design untouched' states the scope, so nothing has to be remembered. minimize_depth would still restructure the whole design and still report a better depth; dropping the basis would additionally leave NAND/NOT behind.

lines.prompt: How tall is the logic behind n8[0] now?
lines.why_hard: The net is named. Dropping the scope returns the design-wide depth -- a much larger and still plausible number.

notes: Values: cone_depth(n8[0])=11, cone_gate_count(n8[0])=63, whole design 1629 gates.
Lines 4 and 5 are scored on params -- both the scope and the basis. Either dropped still yields a plausible-looking success.
Line 6 needs the scope carried from line 5; without it the answer is the design-wide depth.

Every line is self-contained: nothing refers to an earlier turn. The agent sends no conversation history to the model (system = catalog, user = the current line only), so anaphoric wording would test dialogue memory rather than routing.
